summary: Join our comprehensive Responding to Domestic Violence Training Course. Equip yourself with essential tools to address and prevent domestic violence effectively
lede: Domestic violence response training helps professionals recognize abuse and respond safely to disclosures. Designed for people in health, education, social services, HR and community roles, it covers survivor-centred listening, basic risk assessment and safety planning. Participants also practise factual documentation and referrals while considering confidentiality, consent and duty of care.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who may encounter domestic violence in their work and need to respond safely and appropriately.
audience: Health professionals and clinic staff (nurses, doctors
Police, justice, and legal sector staff
Teachers, school counsellors, and education administrators
Public sector staff in social services, gender
Shelter, safe house, and helpline staff
modules: Foundations of Domestic and Gender-Based Violence
Dynamics, Forms, and Impact of Abuse
Recognising Signs, Red Flags, and Risk Indicators
Responding to Disclosures: Survivor-Centred and Trauma-Informed Practice
Working with Children and Young People Affected by Domestic Violence
Vicarious Trauma, Boundaries, and Self-Care for Responders
Case Documentation, Reporting, and Continuous Improvement
prerequisites: Participants should have basic awareness of domestic violence issues and experience in a related professional field. No prior training in domestic violence response is required, but a commitment to learning and engaging with sensitive topics is essential.
